transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, what really pushed me to come in is I’ve been having trouble listening, I guess. Like my wife will be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or who needs a ride, and I’m looking right at her, nodding along, but then a minute later I realize I didn’t actually catch half of what she said. It’s been frustrating.
Can you think of other times recently where you’ve had trouble focusing—not just with your wife talking—but like at work, reading, or even during conversations with friends?

Yeah, it happens other times too. Like if I sit down to work through a catering order, I start out okay, but after a little while my mind just drifts off. Same thing on parish planning calls—I’ll be listening, and then I realize I missed part of it. I end up going back over the same notes again like I never read them in the first place.
Have you noticed your mind wandering like this more when you're feeling down, stressed, or anxious, or does it seem to happen regardless of how you're feeling emotionally?

I’m not really sure, to be honest. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern with my mood. Sometimes I’m stressed, sure, but the drifting off seems to happen even when I don’t feel especially upset or anxious.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in activities you usually enjoy, like during the times when your mind is drifting off?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I get frustrated when I realize I missed something, but I haven’t really noticed feeling hopeless or losing interest in things at the same time. It feels more like my attention just slips.
Have you noticed feeling restless, on edge, or having trouble controlling your worry, especially when your mind starts to drift like this?
Not really, no. I mean, I can get annoyed with myself when I lose track, but I wouldn’t say I feel on edge or like I can’t control worrying. It’s more like my attention just sort of wanders.
Do you find that this issue with your attention drifting happens in other situations outside of work and home, like when you're driving, watching TV, or engaging in hobbies?

Yes, it does happen outside of just work or home stuff. Like if I’m trying to work through a catering order, I’ll start out okay, but then my mind drifts and I have to reread the notes like I didn’t take them in. Same thing if I’m listening to a parish planning call — after a while I realize I’ve missed part of it and have to go back over things.
Have you noticed any other difficulties besides your mind wandering, such as forgetting things, losing items often, or having trouble staying organized?

Yeah, I have noticed some forgetfulness. It’s not constant, but lately I’ll forget things I meant to do, like returning a call from the doctor’s office or picking up a prescription. I’ve also cut it close or left late when I was supposed to get out of the house for one of my cousin’s appointments.
Can you tell me if these issues with attention and forgetfulness happen in different settings, like when you're out with friends, at church, or anywhere else outside of home and work?

Yes, it does. Like I mentioned, if I’m sitting with a catering order, I can start out reading it fine, but then my mind drifts and I have to go back over the same notes again. And on a parish planning call, I’ll be listening, then realize I missed a chunk of what was said. So it’s not just at home.
Looking back, were you someone who had trouble focusing or was easily distracted as a child, maybe in school or during activities?

Yes, I think so. Even back in grade school, before I was 12, I remember teachers telling my parents that I was bright, but that I was always daydreaming. I’d leave homework in my desk, or I’d need reminders to finish my classwork. It was kind of a pattern even then.

Can you describe what happens when your mind starts to drift—do you feel like your thoughts are racing, are you hyper-aware of your surroundings, or does it feel more like you're spacing out and losing track of what’s happening around you?

It’s more like spacing out. I’ll start off following a catering order or listening on a parish planning call, and then after a bit I realize I drifted off. I’m not really racing with thoughts or anything like that — I just lose the thread, and then I have to go back over the notes like I never read them.

Are there times when you’re doing something that you enjoy, like a hobby or watching TV, where you still find your mind drifting or losing focus, or does this mainly happen during tasks that feel like obligations or work?

It’s mostly when it’s something I have to get through, like a catering order or a parish planning call. I’ll start off okay, but then my mind wanders, and I realize I’ve missed part of it. Then I have to go back over the same notes again like I didn’t read them the first time.
Do you also have trouble staying focused during activities that are more casual or social, like conversations with friends, following along at church services, or even just relaxing and watching TV?

Yeah, it can happen in those kinds of settings too, but I notice it most when there’s something I’m supposed to follow along with. Like if I’m listening through a parish planning call, I’ll start out fine, and then after a while I realize I’ve missed pieces of it. Same with working out a catering order—I have to go back over the notes because it’s like I didn’t really take them in the first time.
When you’re going through your day, do you ever notice a background sense of tension or pressure, even if it's not full-blown anxiety, that might be making it harder to focus?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a constant tension or pressure in the background. It feels more like I just lose focus at times, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there feeling anxious or keyed up.
Have you noticed any days where you feel down or lose interest in things for several hours or more, even if it’s not all the time?
I don’t think so, not in a way I’ve really noticed. I mean, I have normal off days, but I can’t say I lose interest in things for hours or feel really down like that.

Can you think of specific examples where this drifting of your attention or forgetfulness has caused problems in your daily life, like missing deadlines, making mistakes at work, or affecting your relationships with others?

Yeah. The main thing is at home. My wife gets frustrated because with helping take care of my cousin, she feels like she can’t always count on me to remember what needs to be done. And with catering stuff, even small jobs, I sometimes have to go back and double-check or redo things so orders don’t get mixed up. It’s not huge every day, but it does cause problems.
Do you find that your mind drifts or you lose focus in settings like driving, being in a crowd, or other situations where staying attentive is important for safety or engagement?

I don’t know that I’d say it happens much with driving or safety stuff. Where I notice it more is if I’m sitting down with a catering order, or trying to listen through a parish planning call. I’ll start off paying attention, but after a while my mind drifts, and then I have to go back over the same notes like I didn’t really read them the first time.
